about.body: The AJ126 is Jaguar Land Rover's 3.0-litre supercharged V6 petrol engine, in production from 2013 to 2020. It shares a 90° V6 architecture with the larger AJ133 5.0-litre V8 and was introduced as a high-performance six-cylinder option across Jaguar's range. The engine appears in the F-Type sports car, the XE and XF saloons, and the flagship XJ. The same supercharged V6 design was used across multiple JLR models, though its application-specific ancillaries, mounting and ECU calibration vary by model and year.

byModel.body: The F-Type was the launch platform for the AJ126, appearing in the V6 (340 hp), V6 S (380 hp) and 400 Sport (400 hp) variants throughout the X152 generation from 2013 to 2020. The XE adopted the same engine for its S and 300 Sport variants (X760, 2015–2019), offering a more sporting saloon option in the range. The XF followed with S and 35t variants (X260, 2015–2018), while the XJ applied the supercharged V6 to its Supersport V6 model (X351, 2013–2019) in markets where a six-cylinder option was preferred over the larger V8.

compatibility.body: Because the AJ126 spans four different Jaguar models — F-Type, XE, XF and XJ — each with different mounting, ancillaries, and ECU calibration, compatibility comes down to confirming your exact model, generation, and year, which we do by registration/VIN. A supercharged V6 from an F-Type isn't a direct match for one from an XJ, even though it's the same base engine code. Ancillaries, mounting, and supercharger tune vary by model and year. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm your exact vehicle.
